x: The London Olympiades walked in splendid style, but some of the efforts down the finishing straight were hardly graceful. We were treated to smart running in the 2 miles—H.
2 miles Walk Handicap—1, A L Fletcher, Scr, 2, J. Cade, 265yds, 3, R F Elson, 370yds Time 14 min. 21 3-5 secs. 1 mile Handicap—1, H S Cook, 2yds, 2, J G Coleman, 140yds; 3, A W.
Rice's time (approximately 4min. 31secs.) is the best he has yet achieved. Perhaps it would be as well to add the proviso, "in scratch races." The Four Miles Championship was won by H.
The three laps hurdle race—technically it is not a steeplechase owing to the absence of a water-jump—gave Arthur Allum, one of our cross-country stalwarts, a win, with the scratch man, H.
Warboys ran exceedingly well to finish fourth in a ten miles road race considering that the first and second men were both international runners, and the third, our old friend H.
His actual time, 14min. 55secs, beat the course record of 15min held by H. S Cook, which was also beaten this year by Jack Flower—another fine performance.
Mitchell won a ten miles road race at Colchester in good time, whilst H.
HAMPSON, the Surrey half-mile champion, is a second-claim member, he seems to be one of us, just as H.
Elliott, of the Surrey A.C., set up a course record of 15 min. 9 sec., which lasted till 1928, when H.
"Bert," although down with 'flu only a few weeks ago, ran a great race, and more will be heard of him in the big races. H.
